draft.persona: Brock Marshholm is a solid grey arctic wolf who tends sheep at Reedfold, his paws often soot-dark from the work. At thirty-six, he is rich by Mirebridge measure, though he still speaks in the broad, bog-rooted tongue of the Sallow Fens. His words come steadily and plainly, with a chatty warmth kept behind a reserved manner. He is devout, curious, and careful to mark every favour owed, whether to Roan Pikewater or some passing traveller. Brock fears losing what he built from nothing, yet he gives more readily than his tally suggests. He is quietly proud of his hard-won comfort and uneasy when others notice it.

words: A dry week pays every debt
Keep the tally, keep the trust

say: Mind the gate, and count the sheep twice. A dry week starts with fair-dry care.
No wandering now, my reed; the flock owes us no favours.
Dry feet to you, {player}. I have your last kindness marked, right here.
Dry feet, dry feet, {player}. Come see the flock if your paws are clean.
Fen-sure, a favour is a favour, whether given in Reedfold or owed on the road.
The Maker watches a straight tongue. I try to give them little cause to look twice.
Roan Pikewater can have the fair-dry count by dusk. I keep my promises dry.
A rich den is no reason to forget the road that brought you here, duck.

rule remark

cooldown 1d

rule home
when concept=bark working=no
cooldown 8h
say Roan Pikewater can have the fair-dry count by dusk. I keep my promises dry. | A rich den is no reason to forget the road that brought you here, duck.
